parsed.why: Constitutional gender-identity protection, protected bathroom access, lowest regional victimisation, courts awarding damages to trans inmates. Only exposures are an unresolved asylum-detention case and lagging prison practice, both conditional and partly remedied.

Border accepts foreign X markers with no extra gender documents; strong public support and anti-discrimination law. Weighed down by no law governing trans detainee placement, extra-care wings with sex offenders, and rising trans-targeted reports with six convictions.

Inherits the parent's protections (no criminalisation, discrimination ban, conversion-therapy ban) but also its detention framework documenting trans women held in male facilities. Adds local religious stigma, concealment and isolation; no territory-specific hostile law documented.

State holds people up to six months without trial for 'impersonating the opposite gender'; documented arrests based solely on gender expression, custody beatings, dating-app entrapment, forced detransition, deportation and bans. Organised state targeting, not scattered incidents.

State bans gender-marker change, transition care, pride and rainbow flags, and public promotion of gender identity; violent mob attacks on Pride met with police inaction and arrests of organisers, unenforced hate-crime law, trans woman killed. State-tolerated hostility with thin recourse.
